title: Machine-learning selection uncovers plant enzymes for alkaloid pathway branches
summary: Support-vector-machine ranking selected poppy homologs whose experimental characterization identified aromatic acetaldehyde synthase activity in PsTyDC6 and phenylpyruvate-decarboxylase activity in PsPDC1. In vitro and engineered E. coli metabolomics detected pathway products including norcoclaurine and reticuline, demonstrating alternative routes from tyrosine into benzylisoquinoline alkaloids.
ai_technology: High-dimensional support vector machine (SVM) enzyme-sequence classifiers
organization: Kobe University, Tokyo Denki University, and collaborators

evidence.tested: Support-vector-machine ranking selected poppy homologs whose experimental characterization identified aromatic acetaldehyde synthase activity in PsTyDC6 and phenylpyruvate-decarboxylase activity in PsPDC1.
evidence.unknown: The study demonstrates enzyme activity and pathway products in vitro and engineered E. coli; it does not establish the exact physiological roles of these enzymes in living poppy plants. The paper describes several enzyme activities as potential and says natural pathway roles need further elucidation.
evidence.ai_role: SVM models ranked more than 100 homologous candidate sequences for specialized aromatic-acetaldehyde-synthase and phenylpyruvate-decarboxylase functions. The team selected high-scoring sequences for in-vitro enzyme assays and metabolomics of reconstructed E. coli pathways.
